title: Cap. V Obj. 6 Sol close: Arminius's foresight-election puts free will under election, not Christ
pass_a_gloss: I add finally, if election were from foresight faith, as Arminius philosophizes, that absurdity would in truth follow which he tries to fasten upon us. For such a law being posited, Whoever will believe will be elected to life, it is plain that men not even existing in the Divine purpose in Christ, but considered in every way outside Christ, by believing merit, or at least from a pact obtain, their election. But to such an election the free choice of each is rather laid under as a foundation, than Christ, when one descends from a universal law to the actual particular election of men.
pass_b_english: Finally: if election were from foresight faith as Arminius philosophizes, the absurdity he tries to pin on us would truly follow. Posit the law Whoever believes will be elected to life — then men not even existing in the divine purpose in Christ, but considered wholly outside Christ, by believing merit or at least by pact obtain their election. Under that election each one's free choice is laid as foundation rather than Christ, when one descends from a universal law to the actual particular election of men.
source_text: Addo denique, si electio esset ex fide praevisa, ut philosophatur Arminius, id absurdi revera sequeretur, quod nobis conatur impingere. Nam posita lege tali, Quisquis credet, ad vitam eligetur, manifestum est homines ne proposito quidem Divino in Christo existentes, sed extra Christum omnimode consideratos, credendo mereri, aut saltem ex pacto consequi, electionem suam. Tali autem electioni liberum uniuscujusque arbitrium fundamenti loco potius substernitur, quam Christus, quando ab universali lege ad actualem particularem hominum electionem descenditur.
